See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Additional classes = ceiling[(Target fraction × Classes held − Attended) ÷ (1 − Target fraction)]

A worked example

You attended 22 of 30 classes and want 75%. Solve (22 + x) ÷ (30 + x) ≥ 0.75 to get x ≥ 2. After two consecutive attended classes, attendance is 24/32 = 75%.

Before you use the result

Assumes every future class counts equally and you attend all of the required consecutive classes. It does not know how many classes remain in your course. If the result exceeds the actual remaining schedule, the target is not achievable that term. After an absence, exactly 100% lifetime attendance cannot be restored.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

What if I already meet the target?

The result is zero additional classes needed to reach it now. Future absences can still lower your attendance.

Does this guarantee enough classes remain?

No. Compare the answer with the published course schedule.
